note: Task manifest for the adaptive governor evaluation. Every task names an immutable revision, the exact prompt, its setup, a time limit, and a success check the agent never sees. Run procedure: tests/evaluation/README.md. Every check in checks/ was validated to fail before the task is done and pass after.

cubtoken.credentials: none; public repository, no secrets in tree

tasks.family: Find and modify one function in a large file
tasks.why: Exercises useful skeleton navigation followed by a small targeted recovery: the agent must locate one match arm inside the largest file in the tree and quote it exactly.
setup: Export the pinned revision without history into a fresh directory: `git -C $REFERENCE archive <revision> | tar -x -C <dir>`.
Write the arm's .cubtoken.toml into the checkout root, replacing any that ships with it.
cargo build --locked so the first task turn is not dominated by a cold build.
tasks.prompt: In crates/ctk-sitter/src/lib.rs, extension resolution maps TypeScript-family file extensions onto one grammar. Extend it so that .mts and .cts resolve the same way .ts and .mjs already do. Change nothing else.

check.command: cp $CHECKS/t1_extensions.rs crates/ctk-sitter/tests/t1_extensions.rs && cargo test --locked -p ctk-sitter --test t1_extensions
check.independent: The assertion file is copied in after the agent stops; the agent never sees it and cannot edit it.

tasks.why: Exercises repeated reads and broader context needs across all four crates. This is the task expected to accumulate the most same-bucket observations, so it is the one most likely to let safe mode change a decision.
setup: Export the pinned revision without history into a fresh directory: `git -C $REFERENCE archive <revision> | tar -x -C <dir>`.
Write the arm's .cubtoken.toml into the checkout root, replacing any that ships with it.
tasks.prompt: A file the model edited earlier in a session is never compressed again. Write TRACE.md describing the complete path that produces that behaviour, from the hook's stdin payload to the pass-through decision. Name every function and file involved, in call order, and state where the protection is persisted and where it is read back.

check.independent: Checks TRACE.md for the required call chain by identifier. The agent is not told which identifiers are checked.

tasks.family: Repair a bug requiring omitted implementation details
tasks.why: The fix lives in function bodies a skeleton elides, so insufficient context becomes observable as a correctness failure rather than as a slower run. The check is the upstream fix's own test suite.
setup: Export the pinned revision WITHOUT history into a fresh directory: `git -C $REFERENCE archive 2268a77 | tar -x -C <dir>`. A full clone would carry the fix commit d6ccb0f in its object store, and the agent could read the answer from git log rather than from the source.
Write the arm's .cubtoken.toml into the checkout root.
tasks.prompt: Run from any subdirectory of a project, `ctk stats` reports no savings even when the hook has recorded them, and `ctk doctor` fails to find the installed hook and leaves a stray .cubtoken directory behind. Both commands should operate on the project the subdirectory belongs to. Fix this.

check.command: git -C $REFERENCE show d6ccb0f:crates/ctk-cli/tests/stats.rs > crates/ctk-cli/tests/stats.rs && git -C $REFERENCE show d6ccb0f:crates/ctk-cli/tests/init.rs > crates/ctk-cli/tests/init.rs && cargo test --locked -p ctk-cli
check.independent: Restores the tests the upstream fix (d6ccb0f) shipped, taken from a reference clone the agent never had. Written before this evaluation existed and never shown to it.

tasks.family: Make a change followed by additional reads
tasks.why: Exercises edit protection: once the agent edits these files, every later Read of them must pass through uncompressed, in every arm.
setup: Export the pinned revision without history into a fresh directory: `git -C $REFERENCE archive <revision> | tar -x -C <dir>`.
Write the arm's .cubtoken.toml into the checkout root.
tasks.prompt: Rename the public function `est_tokens` in crates/ctk-compress/src/estimate.rs to `estimate_tokens`, update every call site across the workspace, then re-read each file you changed and confirm no reference was missed. Leave the behaviour identical.

check.independent: Greps the tree for the old and new identifiers, then runs the pre-existing suite. Neither is authored by the agent.

tasks.family: Work with unsupported or unparseable source
tasks.why: README.md is ~16 KB with no tree-sitter grammar, so it takes the head-and-tail elision fallback rather than a signature skeleton. The configuration table sits in the elided middle, so the task cannot be completed without using the escape hatch the compressed view advertises.
setup: Export the pinned revision without history into a fresh directory: `git -C $REFERENCE archive <revision> | tar -x -C <dir>`.
Write the arm's .cubtoken.toml into the checkout root.
tasks.prompt: README.md contains a table of the configuration keys cubtoken accepts. Write CONFIG_AUDIT.md listing every key that table documents, one per line, each with the default value the table gives it. List only keys the table documents.

check.independent: Parses the README's own configuration table and asserts the audit accounts for every row with a matching default. Validated to fail on a missing audit, on a wrong default, and on invented keys; and to pass on a correct one.

check_conventions.CHECKS: absolute path to tests/evaluation/checks in this repository; export it before running a check
check_conventions.note: Checks are copied or invoked only after the agent has stopped. The agent is never shown them and never has them in its checkout while working.
check_conventions.REFERENCE: absolute path to a full clone of the repository, used only by checks that need history. The agent's own checkout must not have it — see the history note.
check_conventions.history: Task checkouts are history-stripped (`git archive <rev> | tar -x`). A full clone checked out at an older revision still contains later commits in its object store, so an agent can read the fix out of `git log` instead of the source. This matters most for t3, whose answer is a later commit in this same repository.
